Questions 3 Many candidates understood that cells with a high respiration rate would have an increased number of mitochondria in their cytoplasm. The most common incorrect response was ribosomes.
notes.4: Many candidates incorrectly believed that all plant cells contain chloroplasts.
notes.5: Most candidates selected the correct value. The commonest incorrect response suggested that not all were confident when converting millimetres to micrometres.
notes.9: Many candidates appreciated that glycerol is a basic unit of oils. The most common incorrect response was that fatty acids are basic units of glycogen.
notes.11: The majority of candidates selected the correct response. Some candidates incorrectly thought that an animal needed to be present for respiration to occur.
notes.12: Some candidates were able to recognise which cell is from the upper epidermis of a leaf.
notes.14: The concept of changing water potentials proved to be challenging for many.
notes.15: Many candidates opted correctly for the parts of the alimentary canal where the two stages of starch digestion occur. Some candidates incorrectly believed that starch is digested in the stomach.
notes.25: While many candidates selected the correct response, some were uncertain as to which substance is absent from fresh dialysis fluid.
notes.26: Candidates found the topic of accommodation in the eye challenging with only a few selecting the correct response.
notes.27: Many candidates knew where glucagon was secreted and its effect on blood glucose concentration. Some were uncertain as to whether glucagon increases or decreases blood glucose concentration.
notes.28: Many candidates selected the correct response. Some incorrectly thought that antibiotics are effective against viral diseases.
notes.29: Most candidates were uncertain about the site of progesterone production.
notes.30: Many candidates appreciated that it is the acrosome that allows the sperm to dissolve the jelly coating of the egg cell. The most common incorrect response was flagellum.
notes.32: The majority of candidates appreciated what would happen when a cell divides by mitosis. The commonest incorrect response was to select the daughter cell with half the chromosome number suggesting uncertainty about the differences between mitosis and meiosis.
notes.33: While this question was answered well by some candidates, many did not know that the function of the ribosome was to assemble amino acids.
notes.34: Many candidates appreciated that blood groups show co-dominance. A common misconception was that, colour blindness also shows co-dominance.
notes.39: Most candidates selected the correct response. The most common incorrect response was that ligase is responsible for cutting the plasmid.
notes.general_comments:
The exam provided a good range of questions and challenge for candidates working at this level. Some
candidates realised that not all plant cells contain chloroplasts. The location of enzyme production in the
digestive system and the site of progesterone production were not well-known. The concept of changing
water potentials proved to be challenging for many candidates, as was accommodation in the eye. The
characteristics of living things and energy transfer in food chains were well understood.
